analysis:
Integration pass over two prior analyses plus replayed source. Replayed source covers .github/actions/provider-release-build/action.yml, ci.yml, release-dev-branch.yml, release-swift.yml, the changelog, and the ClusterServiceAgent.swift part-health path.

Checked directly:
- The shard input reaches bash only through the SHARD env var, not through expression interpolation in the script. It is regex-validated as K/N with 1<=K<=N and is accepted only on the qualification lane. Outputs index/last/parity are derived numerics or booleans, so I found no injection into GITHUB_OUTPUT or the artifact name.
- Prompt-parity steps now run after the test build and write only counts and logs. The shard artifact uploads only *.json and provider-tests.txt.
- The cluster-worker .build-native-worker directory was added to the Swift cache. The metallib deletion loop was extended to cover it, so a cached metallib cannot be reused.
- Path-filter additions in the two release workflows only widen triggers.
- ClusterServiceAgent.partHealthPath is the fixed filename part-health.json under the service directory, so there is no traversal.

Unit 0 claimed three medium findings: dev-branch signing with the production Developer ID and secrets: inherit, unqualified public cluster placements, and a hardcoded parity qualification. I did not report them. Their cited lines (docs/operations/provider-release.md:527 and :659, ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift:331) are not visible in the supplied replay, and I could not independently verify them or cite a visible line. They remain unresolved and warrant human follow-up. Relevant IDs: A-005, A-011, T-013, T-034, T-054, T-056, A-017, A-001, TB-011.

Other unverified contracts:
- release-provider.yml: whether the sign job gates on the qualify-sdk-shard results and the aggregate audit. Skipped versus failed handling, because the aggregator lacks !cancelled().
- The provider-test-shards.py audit for missing shards.
- Secret and keychain residue when the cluster-runtime facts step runs.
- Coordinator validation of the cluster_runtime block, which is platform-owned.
- The ClusterService.partEnvironment body and the removeEndedApproval hunk.

The threat model has no entry for cluster runtime approval facts, public-model declarations or the dev-branch signing lane, which is a documentation gap. 222 source units were omitted from replay.
